newsitem.title: UK: Zinc hits 10-month high, oil rally looks vulnerable.
newsitem.headline: Zinc hits 10-month high, oil rally looks vulnerable.

text.p: The price of zinc jumped almost three percent to a 10-month high on Tuesday after news of a drop in warehouse stocks of the metal kindled speculator interest.

Elsewhere in commodity markets a long rally in oil prices -- suddenly down by about $1 a barrel -- looked vulnerable to rising supply. But coffee prices extended a rally. Three months zinc rose on the London Metal Exchange to a day's best around $1,110 per tonne in hectic activity.
Floor traders said funds bought zinc after news that LME supervised warehouse stocks declined by 11,975 tonnes to 487,325 in the latest week, the lowest since December 1992.

Zinc's gain of three percent in value from late Monday was registered in spite of selling by China, a key producer of the metal which is used in the galvanising process. "Chinese selling came in at the highs but it should be able to get over $1,100 fairly soon," an LME floor trader said.

Leading brokerage GNI Ltd said in a long-term outlook that zinc might "spike" higher in 1997 as far as $1,240. But GNI added that it also thought a market consensus on a stronger world zinc price this year was overdone.
"Low prices and concentrate shortages have restrained Chinese production in 1996, however, the country's production potential will be enormous over the next few years," GNI said.
Copper was steady and just firmer during Tuesday but aluminium failed to rally above resistance at $1,625 a tonne.

Oil prices were vulnerable after a late sell-off on Monday. February futures for the benchmark Brent Blend of North Sea crude were trading around $23.40 per barrel on Tuesday afternoon or about $1 below where they were on Monday. Oil markets had become jittery at the highs to which they had rallied on cold weather in the United States and Europe, which boosted demand for heating oil, and on low stocks. Prices dived on Monday after forecasts for a new U.S. cold snap were moderated.

The International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Tuesday that revived Iraqi exports and extra oil from sellers outside OPEC had lifted world crude oil supply in December to a record 74.7 million barrels daily, up 1.3 million from November. Coffee futures extended a rally, helped up by news of a drop in U.S. certified stocks. The most active March London robusta contract reached an intra-day high at $1,322 per tonne which was a gain from Monday of $33.

Corn (maize) and soybeans were both firmer in the Chicago futures pits in a continued reaction to recent crop forecasts. Gold closed in London at $357.55 per ounce, weaker than on Monday but above recent 3-1/4 year lows below $354.
Some leading commodity prices at 1645 GMT Tuesday
